questions.question: Name the two most common fuel gasses used for gas welding.
questions.idealAnswer: Oxygen and Acetylene.

questions.question: Name three types of torches used for gas welding.
questions.idealAnswer: Equal pressure, injector and cutting.

questions.question: Why must acetylene gas be kept at 15 psi or below?
questions.idealAnswer: Acetylene gas is very unstable and could explode at higher pressures than 15 psi.

questions.question: What do the cylinders containing Acetylene contain to help stabilize the gas?
questions.idealAnswer: They are packed with a porous material and saturated with acetone to help stabilize the gas.

questions.question: What determines the amount of heat applied to the material being welded in gas welding?
questions.idealAnswer: The size of the tip opening determines the heat applied to the work.

questions.question: What should be considered when selecting a filler welding rod?
questions.idealAnswer: The filler rod selected should be compatible with the base metal being welded.

questions.question: What type of flame should be used when welding aluminum or nickel?
questions.idealAnswer: A carburizing flame should be used when welding non ferrous material such as aluminum, nickel and Monel.

questions.question: What can cause a welding torch to backfire?
questions.idealAnswer: A backfire may be caused by touching the tip against the work, overheating tip, by operating tip at other than recommended pressures. Loose tip or head, dirt or slag in the end of the tip, and may cause molten metal to be splattered when the flame pops.

questions.question: Can a weld bead be filed or ground?
questions.idealAnswer: No, a weld bead should never be filed or ground, this action will cause the weld bead to loose its strength characteristics.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of tack welding.
questions.idealAnswer: A method of holding parts together before welding.

questions.question: What shielding gas is generally used in Gas Tungsten Arc (GTA) welding of aluminum?
questions.idealAnswer: Argon or helium is used in shielding aluminum.

questions.question: In gas Tungsten Arc (GTA) welding, what is the purpose of a stream of inert gas?
questions.idealAnswer: To prevent the formation of oxides in the puddle.

questions.question: When inspecting a butt-weld, the weld penetration should be how thick.
questions.idealAnswer: The weld penetration should be 100 percent of the thickness of the base metal.

questions.question: What is the recommended repair for engine mounts?
questions.idealAnswer: Use a larger diameter replacement tube telescoped over the stub of the original member using fish-mouth and rosette welds.

questions.question: How is the number of beads determined when producing fillet welds in heavy metals?
questions.idealAnswer: The number of beads is determined by the thickness of the metal being welded.

questions.question: What purpose does flux serve in welding aluminum?
questions.idealAnswer: The use of flux in aluminum welding minimizes or prevents oxidation.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to use flux in silver soldering operations?
questions.idealAnswer: The flux removes the film oxide from the base metal and allows the silver solder to stick to it. Also keeps the base metal chemically clean.

questions.question: List the protective personal equipment you should use while welding.
questions.idealAnswer: Welding helmet, welding gloves, protective clothing, and footwear; if not in an adequately ventilated area, appropriate breathing equipment must be used.

questions.question: What color glass is used in protective eye-wear designed especially for aluminum oxy-fuel welding?
questions.idealAnswer: Patented green glass by TM Technologies.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of a cold weld?
questions.idealAnswer: A cold weld has improper penetration and cold laps caused by insufficient heat. It appears rough and irregular , and its edges are not feathered into the metal base .

questions.question: What should be used to make a visual inspection of a weld?
questions.idealAnswer: A magnifying glass of at least 1Ox.

questions.question: Why is Tig preferred over flux welding?
questions.idealAnswer: It produces highest quality weld.

questions.question: How is the inner sleeve tube held in the structural tube until the gap is welded?

questions.question: Why is TIG (GTA) welding preferred over oxyacetylene welding for building and repairing welded steel tube aircraft structure?
questions.idealAnswer: Heat is concentrated in the weld and does not cause as much distortion as gas welding.

questions.question: What is the difference in the appearance of an oxidizing flame, a neutral flame, and a reducing flame produced by an oxyacetylene torch?
questions.idealAnswer: An oxidizing flame has a pointed inner cone and the torch makes a hissing sound. A neutral flame has a rounded inner cone with no ‘feather’ around it. A reducing flame has a definite ‘feather’ around the inner cone.

questions.question: Why must thick plates of metal be preheated before they are welded?
questions.idealAnswer: Controls the expansion and contraction of the metal being welded, and minimizes the stresses when welding thicker metal.

questions.question: Why is it important that all traces of welding flux be removed after a piece of aluminum or magnesium is welded?
questions.idealAnswer: The flux is corrosive and must be removed to keep metal from corrosion.

questions.question: What is the function of the inert gas that is used in TIG (GTA) and MIG (GMA) welding?
questions.idealAnswer: The (inert gas) forms a shield to keep oxygen away from the weld puddle, and prevent oxides from forming which would weaken the weld.

questions.question: Is heat-treated steel normally repairable by welding?

questions.question: What kind of solder is recommended for soldering electrical wires?

questions.question: How much should the bead penetrate the material when welding two pieces of steel with a butt weld?
